title: 1-O-octadecyl-rac-glycerol in WWOX-LoF
summary: A precursor comparison for lipids in first myelin sheaths.

graph.evidence: Red cells restore far more lipid than brain in Pex7-null mice.
graph.inference: The blood response leaves neural delivery and local conversion unresolved.
graph.hypothesis: A local vinyl ether lipid shortage may limit wrapping in some WWOX settings.
graph.experiment: Trace intact precursor into first sheaths and measure conduction.

evidence: After two months, the red-cell C18:0 lipid ratio reached 71% of same-diet WT in Pex7-null mice. Cerebrum reached 0.72%.
inference: The published injury study reported late recovery. Its public treatment workbook uses a transformed scale and cannot reproduce absolute lipid restoration.
hypothesis: If neural vinyl ether lipid supply is limiting, correcting it may improve first sheaths when downstream conversion and axon eligibility are preserved.
experiment: Compare barrier and direct recipient access in matched WWOX preparations. Track labeled absolute alkyl and vinyl ether products in persistent first sheaths and read conduction.
limits: Age-specific delivery, tolerability and native WWOX lipid deficiency are unresolved. Retain a local research comparator and defer systemic pediatric priority.
